clips.send: The Manila galleons (Spain). 1565–1815. American silver across the Pacific to buy Chinese silk and porcelain. Each year Spanish galleons sailed between Acapulco (Mexico) and Manila (Philippines). They carried silver mined in Mexico and Peru; Chinese merchants in Manila traded silk and porcelain for it. A huge share of the world’s silver flowed to Ming China — and the Ming began collecting taxes in silver.

clips.send: Bartolomeu Dias (Portugal). 1487–1488. First European to sail round the southern tip of Africa. Portugal had crept down Africa’s coast for 70 years, looking for gold and a sea road to Asian spices. A storm blew Dias’s two caravels far south; turning east, then north, he found the coast running east — Africa had an end! His tired crew made him turn back. The king renamed the “Cape of Storms” the Cape of Good Hope.

clips.send: Zheng He (China, Ming). 7 voyages, 1405–1433. “Down to the Western Oceans” with the biggest wooden fleet of its time. The first voyage: 62 large “treasure ships” and over 27,800 men (Ming History); 200+ ships in all are often quoted. Over 28 years the fleet visited 30+ countries and regions of Asia and Africa — as far as the east coast of Africa and the Red Sea. It carried silk and porcelain and brought back spices, gems — and a giraffe for the emperor (1414). Goal: show the Ming emperor’s power and build friendly “tribute” ties — not conquest or colonies. The voyages stopped after 1433.

clips.send: Magellan and Elcano (sailing for Spain). 1519–1522. The first voyage all the way around the world. Five ships and about 270 men left Spain in 1519 to reach the Spice Islands by sailing west. They found a stormy passage at South America’s tip (the Strait of Magellan) and entered an ocean so calm Magellan called it the “Pacific”. The crossing took about 98 days; the crew ate leather and sawdust, and scurvy killed many. Magellan was killed in 1521 in a battle on Mactan in the Philippines. Juan Sebastián Elcano brought the last ship, the Victoria, home with 18 men in 1522.

clips.send: The Atlantic “triangle trade”. 1500s–1860s. Goods, Africa; enslaved people, Americas; sugar, cotton, silver, Europe. Outward: European ships carried cloth, guns and metal goods to West Africa. Middle passage: about 12.5 million Africans were forced onto slave ships; about 10.7 million survived the crossing (Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database). Homeward: sugar, tobacco, cotton and silver made in the Americas went back to Europe. Africa lost millions of young people; enslaved people and their descendants built much of the Americas’ wealth.

clips.send: Christopher Columbus (sailing for Spain). 1492–1493. Sailed west to reach Asia — and reached the Americas. An Italian from Genoa, paid by Spain’s Queen Isabella and King Ferdinand. Three ships: Niña, Pinta and Santa María. He believed Earth was round (true) but much smaller than it is (false) — he thought Japan was about where America is. 12 October 1492: landing in the Bahamas, home of the Taíno people. He called them “Indians” because he thought he was in the Indies. His voyages began Spanish conquest and colonies; Taíno numbers collapsed from disease, forced labour and violence.

clips.send: Vasco da Gama (Portugal). 1497–1499 (India: May 1498). Opened the sea road from Europe to India. Four ships, about 170 men. In the South Atlantic he swung far out to sea — about 3 months without seeing land. In East Africa (Malindi) he took on a local pilot who knew the monsoon winds across the Indian Ocean. He reached Calicut, India, in May 1498. Only about 55 of his men made it home — many died of scurvy. The pepper and spices he brought back paid for the voyage many times over.

clips.send: 达·伽马（葡萄牙）。1497—1499年（1498年5月到达印度）。开辟了从欧洲到印度的新航路。4艘船、约170人。在南大西洋他远离海岸航行，约3个月看不到陆地。在东非的马林迪，他请到一位熟悉印度洋季风的当地领航员。1498年5月到达印度的卡利卡特。只有约55人活着回国，许多人死于坏血病。带回的胡椒和香料，价值是这次航行费用的许多倍。

clips.send: 麦哲伦与埃尔卡诺（为西班牙航行）。1519—1522年。人类第一次环球航行。1519年，5艘船、约270人从西班牙出发，想向西航行到达香料群岛。他们在南美洲南端找到一条风浪险恶的海峡（麦哲伦海峡），驶入一片平静的大洋，麦哲伦称之为“太平洋”。横渡太平洋用了约98天，船员吃皮革和木屑，许多人死于坏血病。1521年，麦哲伦在菲律宾的马克坦岛与当地人作战时被杀。埃尔卡诺率领最后一艘船“维多利亚号”和18个人于1522年回到西班牙。

clips.send: 大西洋“三角贸易”。16—19世纪。商品运往非洲；被奴役的人运往美洲；糖、棉花、金银运回欧洲。出程：欧洲船把布匹、枪支和金属制品运往西非。中程：约1250万非洲人被强行押上奴隶船，约1070万人活着到达美洲（“跨大西洋奴隶贸易数据库”估计）。归程：把美洲生产的糖、烟草、棉花和金银运回欧洲。非洲失去了数以百万计的青壮年；被奴役者和他们的后代为美洲创造了大量财富。

clips.send: 马尼拉大帆船（西班牙）。1565—1815年。把美洲白银运过太平洋，换取中国丝绸和瓷器。西班牙大帆船每年往返于墨西哥的阿卡普尔科和菲律宾的马尼拉。船上装着墨西哥和秘鲁开采的白银；中国商人在马尼拉用丝绸和瓷器换取白银。世界上很大一部分白银流入明代中国，明朝开始用白银征税。

clips.send: 迪亚士（葡萄牙）。1487—1488年。第一个绕过非洲南端的欧洲航海家。葡萄牙人沿非洲海岸向南探索了约70年，寻找黄金和通往亚洲香料产地的海路。风暴把迪亚士的两艘轻快帆船吹到很远的南方；他向东、再向北航行，发现海岸线转向东方——非洲到头了！疲惫的船员逼他返航。国王把“风暴角”改名为“好望角”。

clips.send: 哥伦布（为西班牙航行）。1492—1493年。想向西到达亚洲，却到达了美洲。他是意大利热那亚人，受西班牙女王伊莎贝拉和国王斐迪南资助，率“尼尼亚号”“平塔号”“圣玛利亚号”三艘船出发。他相信地球是圆的（对），但把地球想得太小（错）——他以为日本就在美洲的位置。1492年10月12日，他在巴哈马群岛登陆，那里住着泰诺人。他以为到了“印度”，就把当地人叫作“印第安人”。他的航行开启了西班牙的征服和殖民；泰诺人因疾病、强迫劳动和暴力而大量死亡。

clips.send: 郑和（中国·明朝）。七次下西洋，1405—1433年。率领当时世界上规模最大的木帆船队“下西洋”。第一次出航有大宝船62艘、2.78万余人（《明史》），全部船只常说有200多艘。28年间到访亚非30多个国家和地区，最远到达非洲东海岸和红海沿岸。船队带去丝绸、瓷器，带回香料、宝石，1414年还带回一头长颈鹿献给皇帝。目的：宣扬明朝国威，加强与亚非国家的友好往来和朝贡贸易，不是征服和殖民。1433年以后不再远航。
